title: Neurons as an Interpretable Basis
summary: Neural networks have long been regarded as opaque black boxes, in part because their neurons seemed inscrutable. This article makes the case that language model neurons—the hidden units of MLPs—are interpretable units of computation.

title: FOVI-Dex: Foveation enables efficient perceptive learning of dexterous manipulation in simulation
summary: FOVI-Dex: Foveation enables efficient perceptive learning of dexterous manipulation in simulation Advanced physics simulators and rendering engines promise to support the next-generation of robotic reinforcement learning (RL), yet training perceptive policies remains challenging due to the high-costs of rendering and perception. We propose foveation as a solution to this challenge, coupling a novel foveated rendering solution with foveated perception, alongside a careful approach for ensuring transfer to foveated sampling of real uniform cameras. We train a language-conditioned visuotactile policy controlling a dexterous arm-hand to find and grasp a target object in clutter (FOVI-Dex), via online RL without demonstrations. In comparison to a high-resolution fixed-camera control, FOVI-Dex uses 8.9 less vision tokens, supporting 6 more parallel environments and 4.4 higher training throughput. At matched training budgets, this efficiency enables FOVI-Dex to outperform both the high-resolution baseline and a matched uniform active camera baseline, in both sim and real, with an outsized advantage in the real world. jaehyunj Mon, 11/09/2026 - 19:17

title: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember
summary: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember Meta AI just launched their entry in the Claude Haiku/GPT Luna category: Muse Ember, which they describe as: [...] our smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing. For shorter prompts it's priced the same as GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 - both are $0.10/million input tokens and $0.50/million output. Today's other big model release, Claude Fable 5.2, is 80x that price at $8/$40. The pricing is a little less straightforward as prompts get longer, though. Luna, Ember, and Haiku all support up to a million input tokens, but they also all have a threshold after which the price goes up. Taking that threshold into account Ember is priced between the two others: Model Prompt size Input ($/M) Cached input Output GPT-6 Luna ≤272k $0.10 $0.01 $0.50 >272k $0.20 $0.02 $0.75 Muse Ember 1.0 ≤200k $0.10 $0.004 $0.50 >200k $0.30 $0.012 $1.50 Claude Haiku 5.5 ≤100k $0.10 $0.01 $0.50 >100k $0.50 $0.05 $2.50 But comparing price-per-token doesn't really make sense these days, when reasoning tokens mean that different models might use dramatically different numbers of tokens to solve the same problem.
